source.title: Updating the standard neuron model in artificial neural networks
source.authors: Raúl Mohedano; Thomas Batard; Erik Velasco-Salido; Ramsses De Los Santos Mendoza; Jorge H. Martínez; Stacey Levine; Marcelo Bertalmío

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including Methods and Supplementary Information.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own comparison of a modified neuron architecture with a standard-neuron network, including a noisy-label experiment it interprets as reduced memorization. This refines the scope of memorization and generalization claims but does not test random-label interpolation or the listed optimizer, batch-size, dropout, or generalization-measure claims.
record.gate_note: Relevant reported outcomes are the validation-accuracy comparisons under label corruption (Fig. 8) and the authors' explicit curvature analysis of memorization. Other experiments concern data efficiency, robustness, expressivity, and learning speed; cited results are not extracted. Fig. 8 provides plotted values without exact numerical values in the text, so the rows record its stated qualitative result.
record.test_reason: The study compares a proposed neuron model with standard neurons but tests none of V1–V8. Validation accuracy with partially corrupted labels does not establish random-label fitting capacity (V1), and input-loss curvature does not measure magnitude-aware weight sharpness or its association with generalization gaps (V7). Figure 6 varies width but provides neither interpolation thresholds nor training-to-convergence evidence required for V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' memorization conclusion: they interpret improved peak validation accuracy under label corruption and conditionally lower estimated input-loss curvature as evidence of reduced memorization. These results do not directly establish reduced fitting of corrupted labels. Their broader conclusion also includes improved expressivity, robustness, learning speed, and data efficiency.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a new implicit-bias neuron with standard neurons, using SGD on image classification tasks; its label-corruption experiment evaluates maximum validation accuracy rather than random-label interpolation or test error after fitting random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and the proportion of scrambled training labels; the text says the advantage is larger with mislabeled data and, in some instances, widens as the wrong-label proportion increases.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report a larger IBNN advantage in maximum validation accuracy when some training labels are scrambled, with the advantage sometimes widening as corruption increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed neuron model improves peak validation accuracy relative to standard neurons under partial training-label corruption on Fashion-MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR-10. Reduced memorization is the authors' interpretation, rather than a directly measured fitting rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated approximations, estimated input-loss curvature scales by (1 + λp)² and decreases when |1 + λp| < 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitable implicit-bias parameters can reduce estimated input-loss curvature relative to standard neurons under the derivation's assumptions.

record.problems: Fig. 8 reports plotted results without exact values in the text; the comparison uses different numbers of independent instances (10 SM and 5 IBNN for memorization), and its uncertainty intervals are 90% CIs. The curvature result depends on multiple analytical approximations and is not an empirical test of a generalization gap.
record.rows_left_out: No separate result rows omitted. Fig. 8 exact plotted values are not recoverable from the supplied text, so only qualitative outcome is recorded in the associated finding; other paper results do not test the listed versions.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect fixed-random-label training fit and natural-label generalization, with chance held-out accuracy for random labels.
Test-error behavior beyond the width needed for zero training error. Figure 6 reports validation accuracy across channel counts without establishing interpolation or convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; all reported classifier training uses SGD.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, including interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness as a predictor of generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version, but no verdict labels apply because none is tested. Its citation of Feldman and Zhang does not test V8. Exact Figure 8 values are unavailable in the supplied text; the qualitative comparison is explicitly stated.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label held-out accuracy comparison.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold with test error measured.
The comparisons change neuron model within convolutional networks; they do not compare convolutional with fully connected networks.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of generalization-gap measures.
No removal of influential memorized examples and retraining.

rows.operation_detail: Derived a relationship between input-loss gradients and estimated input curvature under stated approximations.

conditions.value: ReLU outer activation; network assumed in its linear range
uniform wik=1/D; sparse filters with bounded elements
piece-wise linear σ with central slope p

rows.measure: Estimated loss curvature w.r.t. input, as a measure of memorization
rows.value: CurvIBNN(x) = (1 + λp)² CurvSM(x); authors state IBNN memorizes less when |1 + λp|<1
rows.note: The result is a theoretical derivation under explicit approximations and a parameter condition, not a direct test-error-gap measurement.
rows.check: Change partial to cannot_determine: this conditional analytical approximation concerns input-loss curvature, not a listed version's effect. The curvature scaling inherits the derivation's approximations and is not an empirical measurement of memorization, weight sharpness, or generalization gaps.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
